parts.title: The World in 2026: Country Summaries, Part 1 (Rewritten)

entities.name: Afghanistan
entities.snapshot: Pakistan bombed Kabul and Kandahar in 2026 and declared "open war" on the Taliban, accusing it of sheltering militants who attack Pakistani soldiers.

entities.name: Angola
entities.snapshot: An oil state still governed by the MPLA, the movement that won the 1975 to 2002 civil war, with a young, fast-growing and increasingly restless population.

entities.name: Albania
entities.snapshot: Edi Rama won a fourth term in 2025 and is racing to join the EU by 2030, in a country that emptied out through emigration after communism.

entities.name: Andorra
entities.snapshot: A Pyrenean microstate with two princes, France's president and the Bishop of Urgell, that is negotiating closer ties with the EU while managing a housing squeeze.

entities.name: United Arab Emirates
entities.snapshot: Iran fired more missiles and drones at the UAE than at any other country, hitting Dubai landmarks and shaking the region's safe-harbour reputation.

entities.name: Argentina
entities.snapshot: Javier Milei's chainsaw austerity crushed inflation and won him a labour reform in 2026, but factories and shops are shrinking and jobs are now the top worry.

entities.name: Armenia
entities.snapshot: Nikol Pashinyan won a third term outright in June 2026 on the promise of peace with Azerbaijan, after clashing with the Armenian Church.

entities.name: Antigua and Barbuda
entities.snapshot: A twin-island Caribbean state built on tourism, led by Gaston Browne, who is pushing for reparations for slavery and has floated becoming a republic.

entities.name: Australia
entities.snapshot: Pauline Hanson's One Nation overtook the Liberals in the polls in 2026, cracking Australia's two-party system even as Labor kept its lead head to head.

entities.name: Austria
entities.snapshot: Austerity in a recession left the centrist coalition deeply unpopular, with the far-right FPÖ polling near 34 percent and its leader Herbert Kickl far ahead as preferred chancellor.

entities.name: Azerbaijan
entities.snapshot: Three years after retaking Karabakh, Ilham Aliyev is finalising a US-brokered peace with Armenia that includes a US-run transit route across Armenian territory.

entities.name: Burundi
entities.snapshot: One of the world's poorest countries, dominated by the ruling CNDD-FDD, which won every elected seat in 2025, and drawn into the Congo war next door.

entities.name: Belgium
entities.snapshot: Wave after wave of general strikes hit Belgium in 2026 against pension cuts and limits on wage indexation by Bart De Wever's five-party coalition.

entities.name: Benin
entities.snapshot: The country that pioneered peaceful handovers in Africa held another in 2026, but with the main opposition kept off the ballot and jihadist attacks spreading in the north.

entities.name: Burkina Faso
entities.snapshot: A junta led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, Africa's youngest leader, which has turned to Russia and stretched its rule to 2029 while jihadists control large parts of the country.

entities.name: Bangladesh
entities.snapshot: The February 2026 election, the first since the student uprising that toppled Sheikh Hasina, gave Tarique Rahman's BNP a landslide and ended Muhammad Yunus's interim rule.

entities.name: Bulgaria
entities.snapshot: Former president Rumen Radev won Bulgaria's first single-party majority since 1997 in April 2026, promising to dismantle the "mafia state" after seven elections in four years.

entities.name: Bahrain
entities.snapshot: Hit hard by Iranian missiles aimed at the US Fifth Fleet, Bahrain's Sunni monarchy answered sympathy for Iran among its Shia majority with mass arrests.

entities.name: Bahamas
entities.snapshot: A tourism and offshore finance archipelago where Philip Davis won a rare second consecutive term for his party in a May 2026 snap election.

entities.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
entities.snapshot: Bosnia's October 2026 election largely kept the same nationalist-led balance, while the Serb entity's former leader Milorad Dodik still pulls strings after being barred from office.

entities.name: Belarus
entities.snapshot: Alexander Lukashenko has been trading political prisoners for US sanctions relief, while staying firmly in Russia's camp and hosting its nuclear weapons.

entities.name: Belize
entities.snapshot: Central America's only English-speaking country, where Johnny Briceño won a landslide second term in 2025 and a border claim by Guatemala is before the World Court.

entities.name: Bolivia
entities.snapshot: The first non-MAS president in two decades scrapped fuel subsidies and turned to the IMF to stop an economic collapse that left queues at petrol stations.

entities.name: Brazil
entities.snapshot: Flávio Bolsonaro beat the polls to top the October 2026 first round against Lula, setting up a runoff on 25 October between the two camps that have defined Brazil.

entities.name: Barbados
entities.snapshot: A republic since 2021, where Mia Mottley, a leading global voice on climate finance, won a third term in February 2026 by sweeping all 30 seats.

entities.name: Brunei
entities.snapshot: A small, oil-rich sultanate on Borneo ruled by Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, one of the world's longest-reigning monarchs, under a strict Islamic legal code.

entities.name: Bhutan
entities.snapshot: The Himalayan kingdom of Gross National Happiness, now trying to stem an exodus of young people with a new mindfulness city on the Indian border.

entities.name: Botswana
entities.snapshot: One of Africa's most stable democracies, now led by its first opposition government and searching for a future beyond diamonds as global demand slumps.

entities.name: Central African Republic
entities.snapshot: A diamond- and gold-rich country with very weak state control, where Russian forces guard the government and President Touadéra won a third term after rewriting the constitution.

entities.name: Canada
entities.snapshot: Canada walked out of trade talks and hit back with tariffs of its own after Trump imposed 50 percent duties, with three in four Canadians backing the fight.

entities.name: Switzerland
entities.snapshot: A rich, neutral federation run by consensus and direct democracy, which struck a deal in 2025 to cut punishing US tariffs on its exports.

entities.name: Chile
entities.snapshot: José Antonio Kast, a hard-right former congressman, took office in March 2026 promising to seal the northern border and deport irregular migrants.

entities.name: China
entities.snapshot: Xi Jinping's purge reached the top of the army in 2026, when China's senior general was put under investigation, as Beijing bet its new five-year plan on chips and AI.

entities.name: Côte d'Ivoire
entities.snapshot: The world's biggest cocoa producer began 2026 with Alassane Ouattara starting a fourth term at 84, after his strongest challengers were kept off the ballot.

entities.name: Cameroon
entities.snapshot: Ruled since 1982 by Paul Biya, now in his 90s and declared winner of an eighth term in 2025, while an Anglophone separatist conflict grinds on in the west.

entities.name: DR Congo
entities.snapshot: Peace deals signed in Washington and Doha in 2025 did not end the war in the east, where Rwanda-backed M23 rebels still run Goma and Bukavu and the mines around them.

entities.name: Republic of the Congo
entities.snapshot: Denis Sassou Nguesso, in power for most of the past four decades, won another term in 2026 in an election held with the internet switched off.

entities.name: Colombia
entities.snapshot: Colombia swung from its first leftist president to Abelardo de la Espriella, a millionaire lawyer who promised a Bukele-style crackdown on armed groups.

entities.name: Comoros
entities.snapshot: An Indian Ocean island nation that has seen some 20 coups and attempts since 1975, now dominated by Azali Assoumani, who is grooming his son to follow him.

entities.name: Cape Verde
entities.snapshot: An Atlantic island democracy with a long record of peaceful handovers; in May 2026 voters swapped governments again, bringing the PAICV back to power.

entities.name: Costa Rica
entities.snapshot: Laura Fernández, a protégé of the outgoing populist president, won in the first round in February 2026 on a promise to fight the rising drug violence.

entities.name: Cuba
entities.snapshot: A US oil blockade after the fall of Maduro collapsed Cuba's power grid several times in 2026, leaving millions in the dark and sparking rare protests.

entities.name: Cyprus
entities.snapshot: The far-right ELAM doubled its seats in May 2026's parliamentary election, and a YouTuber's new party got in too, as Cyprus held the EU presidency.

entities.name: Czechia
entities.snapshot: Billionaire Andrej Babiš returned as prime minister with the hard right, promising "not a crown" of Czech money for Ukraine, while President Petr Pavel acts as a check.

entities.name: Germany
entities.snapshot: The far-right AfD won nearly 44 percent in Saxony-Anhalt in September 2026, three seats short of a majority, a heavy blow to Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

entities.name: Djibouti
entities.snapshot: A tiny Red Sea port state that hosts American, Chinese, French and Japanese bases, where Ismaïl Omar Guelleh won a sixth term in 2026 with 97.8 percent.

entities.name: Dominica
entities.snapshot: The "nature island" of the Caribbean, rebuilt after Hurricane Maria in 2017 with a plan to become the first climate-resilient nation, led by Roosevelt Skerrit since 2004.

entities.name: Denmark
entities.snapshot: Mette Frederiksen's snap election backfired with her party's worst result in 120 years, but she clung on in a third government with Lars Løkke Rasmussen as kingmaker.

entities.name: Dominican Republic
entities.snapshot: The Caribbean's fastest-growing big economy, run by Luis Abinader, whose hard line on Haitian migrants is popular at home and criticised abroad.

entities.name: Algeria
entities.snapshot: Africa's largest country by area, run by an army-backed presidency that outlasted the 2019 Hirak protests and pays for social peace with gas money.

entities.name: Ecuador
entities.snapshot: Daniel Noboa took his war on gangs across the border, launching joint operations with the US and slapping punishing tariffs on Colombia.

entities.name: Egypt
entities.snapshot: The Iran war hit Egypt's three cash machines at once, the Suez Canal, tourism and foreign investment, as Sisi tried to stay out of the fight and act as mediator.

entities.name: Eritrea
entities.snapshot: One of the world's most closed states, ruled since independence in 1993 by Isaias Afwerki with no elections, no constitution in force and indefinite military service.

entities.name: Spain
entities.snapshot: A housing protest movement camped in Madrid's Puerta del Sol, and after parliament rejected his emergency decrees, Pedro Sánchez called a snap election for 29 November.

entities.name: Estonia
entities.snapshot: The digital republic on NATO's eastern edge elected a new president, constitutional watchdog Ülle Madise, in 2026, while its governing coalition struggles in the polls.

entities.name: Ethiopia
entities.snapshot: Abiy Ahmed's party took nearly 90 percent of seats in a June 2026 election held amid a crackdown, with insurgencies still burning in Amhara and Oromia.

entities.name: Finland
entities.snapshot: NATO's newest frontline state, which joined in 2023 after decades of neutrality, now led by a right-wing coalition cutting spending as unemployment rises.

entities.name: Fiji
entities.snapshot: Two deputy prime ministers were charged by the anti-corruption agency in 2026, shaking former coup leader Sitiveni Rabuka's coalition ahead of the next election.

entities.name: France
entities.snapshot: Sébastien Lecornu survived as prime minister and passed a budget, as the race to succeed Macron in 2027 opened with the far right in its strongest position ever.

entities.name: Micronesia
entities.snapshot: A federation of four island states spread across the western Pacific, tied to the US by a renewed compact and courted by China.

entities.name: Gabon
entities.snapshot: The general who ended 56 years of Bongo family rule in a 2023 coup won the 2025 presidential election by a landslide and abolished the post of prime minister.

entities.name: United Kingdom
entities.snapshot: Keir Starmer resigned in June 2026 after a local election rout, and Labour handed the keys to Andy Burnham, Britain's seventh prime minister in ten years.

entities.name: Georgia
entities.snapshot: Georgian Dream moved to ban the three biggest opposition parties and jailed protesters, as the country's EU dream receded and it drifted toward Moscow.

entities.name: Ghana
entities.snapshot: One of West Africa's steadiest democracies spent 2026 recovering from a debt default, with John Mahama promising a round-the-clock economy to create jobs.

entities.name: Guinea
entities.snapshot: General Mamadi Doumbouya, who seized power in 2021, turned himself into an elected president in December 2025 under a new constitution written by his junta.

entities.name: Gambia
entities.snapshot: Mainland Africa's smallest country, a sliver along the Gambia River, where Adama Barrow is seeking a third term in the 5 December 2026 election.

entities.name: Guinea-Bissau
entities.snapshot: The army seized power in November 2025 on the eve of election results, the latest of many coups in a country known as a cocaine transit hub.

entities.name: Equatorial Guinea
entities.snapshot: Ruled since 1979 by Teodoro Obiang, the world's longest-serving president, whose family controls an oil economy that has left most citizens poor.

entities.name: Greece
entities.snapshot: A fraud scandal over EU farm subsidies, centred on Crete, led to indictments of lawmakers from Mitsotakis's own party and dented his government.

entities.name: Grenada
entities.snapshot: The "spice isle" of the Caribbean, governed since 2022 by Dickon Mitchell and still rebuilding Carriacou after Hurricane Beryl.

entities.name: Guatemala
entities.snapshot: The exit of attorney general Consuelo Porras in May 2026 ended a long siege on Bernardo Arévalo's anti-corruption presidency, with barely a year left before the 2027 election.

entities.name: Guyana
entities.snapshot: An oil boom has made Guyana's economy the world's fastest-growing, and Irfaan Ali won a second term in 2025 promising to share the wealth, while Venezuela claims two-thirds of its land.

entities.name: Honduras
entities.snapshot: Nasry Asfura, endorsed by Trump days before the vote, took office in January 2026 after a disputed count returned the National Party to power.

entities.name: Croatia
entities.snapshot: A tourism-driven euro member where the conservative HDZ governs with nationalist partners, while the president, Zoran Milanović, plays a combative opposition role.

entities.name: Haiti
entities.snapshot: With gangs controlling most of Port-au-Prince and the transitional council's mandate expired, an unelected prime minister became Haiti's sole ruler in 2026.

entities.name: Hungary
entities.snapshot: Péter Magyar's Tisza party ended Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule in April 2026 with the biggest majority in Hungary's post-communist history.

entities.name: Indonesia
entities.snapshot: Fuel price rises triggered by the Iran war brought students back onto the streets against Prabowo Subianto, whose free school meals programme has become a lightning rod.

entities.name: India
entities.snapshot: Modi's BJP finally captured West Bengal in 2026, while a film star's new party broke Tamil Nadu's 50-year duopoly, redrawing India's federal map.

entities.name: Ireland
entities.snapshot: A rich, fast-growing country dependent on US tech and pharma giants, where a housing crisis dominates politics and a left-wing independent won the presidency in 2025.

entities.name: Iran
entities.snapshot: Ali Khamenei was killed in the opening hours of the US-Israeli assault in February; his son took over, and Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz shook the world economy.

entities.name: Iraq
entities.snapshot: Iraq became a battlefield again as Iran-aligned militias traded fire with US forces, and it took until April to elect a president and pick a prime minister after the 2025 election.

entities.name: Iceland
entities.snapshot: Icelanders narrowly voted against reopening EU membership talks in August 2026, even as Trump's Greenland threats made them question their security.

entities.name: Israel
entities.snapshot: Israelis vote on 27 October 2026 in the first election after a full term since 1988, with Naftali Bennett leading a merged opposition against Benjamin Netanyahu.

entities.name: Italy
entities.snapshot: Giorgia Meloni lost her first big vote when Italians rejected her judicial reform in a March 2026 referendum, setting up a tense run to the 2027 election.

entities.name: Jamaica
entities.snapshot: Jamaica spent 2026 rebuilding its western parishes after Hurricane Melissa, among the strongest Atlantic storms on record to make landfall.

entities.name: Jordan
entities.snapshot: Iranian missiles crossed Jordan's skies and targeted a US-used base, its Israeli gas supply was cut, and tourism slumped, yet the war raised the kingdom's strategic value.

entities.name: Japan
entities.snapshot: Sanae Takaichi, Japan's first woman prime minister, won a two-thirds supermajority in a February 2026 snap election, the LDP's biggest win ever, on a hard line toward Beijing.

entities.name: Kazakhstan
entities.snapshot: A new constitution, rushed to a referendum in March 2026, replaced parliament with a single chamber and restored a vice president, while handing Tokayev new powers.

entities.name: Kenya
entities.snapshot: The 2027 race has started early: Ruto's sacked deputy Rigathi Gachagua now leads a united opposition trying to take his Mount Kenya votes away.

entities.name: Kyrgyzstan
entities.snapshot: Sadyr Japarov broke with his powerful security chief in 2026, and a court later convicted the former ally of plotting to seize power.

entities.name: Cambodia
entities.snapshot: A cold peace followed the deadly 2025 border war with Thailand, while Cambodia's scam compounds, which hold trafficked workers, drew global crackdowns.

entities.name: Kiribati
entities.snapshot: Atolls spread across an ocean area the size of India, among the most exposed to rising seas, governed by Taneti Maamau, who switched recognition from Taiwan to China.

entities.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
entities.snapshot: The smallest country in the Americas, a two-island federation financed largely by selling citizenship to foreign investors.

entities.name: South Korea
entities.snapshot: Courts sentenced former president Yoon Suk Yeol to life for his 2024 martial law attempt, then added 30 years for a plot to provoke North Korea.

entities.name: Kuwait
entities.snapshot: With parliament suspended, Kuwait's emir has stripped more than 71,000 people of citizenship and abolished naturalisation, redefining who counts as Kuwaiti.

entities.name: Laos
entities.snapshot: A one-party communist state heavily in debt to China, whose 2026 party congress and assembly vote kept the same leadership in place.

entities.name: Lebanon
entities.snapshot: Lebanon was dragged back into war when Hezbollah fired on Israel after the strikes on Iran, wrecking the new government's year of reclaiming sovereignty.

entities.name: Liberia
entities.snapshot: Africa's oldest republic, founded by freed American slaves, governed since 2024 by Joseph Boakai after a peaceful handover from George Weah.

entities.name: Libya
entities.snapshot: Split between rival governments since 2014, Libya saw fighting shut its biggest refinery in 2026 before the two sides agreed to hold elections within two years.

entities.name: Saint Lucia
entities.snapshot: A volcanic island of the Pitons, governed by Philip J. Pierre's Labour Party, re-elected in December 2025.

entities.name: Liechtenstein
entities.snapshot: An Alpine principality where the prince retains real power, the economy runs on finance and industry, and the head of government has been a woman since 2025.

entities.name: Sri Lanka
entities.snapshot: Sri Lanka is rebuilding after Cyclone Ditwah, thought to be more destructive than the 2004 tsunami, without breaking the fragile recovery from its 2022 default.

entities.name: Lesotho
entities.snapshot: A mountain kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, dependent on water exports and textile jobs that were hit by US tariffs in 2025.

entities.name: Lithuania
entities.snapshot: A NATO frontline state hosting a permanent German brigade, governed by a Social Democrat-led coalition whose inclusion of a populist party has caused repeated rows.

entities.name: Luxembourg
entities.snapshot: Europe's richest country per head, a Grand Duchy that welcomed a new monarch, Grand Duke Guillaume, in October 2025.

entities.name: Latvia
entities.snapshot: Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs's United List won a record 42 of 100 seats in the October 2026 election, as a party opposed to aiding Ukraine also gained.

entities.name: Morocco
entities.snapshot: A September 2026 election produced Morocco's first woman head of government, while real power stays with the king and a Gen Z protest movement demands better schools and hospitals.

entities.name: Monaco
entities.snapshot: The world's most densely populated country, a tax haven for the very rich ruled by the Grimaldi family since 1297.

entities.name: Moldova
entities.snapshot: Maia Sandu's pro-EU government is pushing for membership by 2028, helped by Orbán's fall, while the Russian-backed region of Transnistria rations gas.

entities.name: Madagascar
entities.snapshot: Gen Z protests over water and power cuts brought down President Rajoelina in 2025, and an army colonel now runs a transition that promises elections.

entities.name: Maldives
entities.snapshot: An Indian Ocean archipelago of luxury resorts and rising seas, led by Mohamed Muizzu, who has balanced between India and China while grappling with heavy debt.

entities.name: Mexico
entities.snapshot: Mexican forces killed the boss of the Jalisco cartel in 2026, but a US indictment of a sitting governor from Sheinbaum's own party showed the pressure only growing.

entities.name: Marshall Islands
entities.snapshot: A US-allied atoll nation still living with the legacy of 67 American nuclear tests, which renewed its compact with Washington in 2024.

entities.name: North Macedonia
entities.snapshot: A nationalist-led government has stalled EU talks by refusing Bulgaria's demand to recognise a Bulgarian minority in the constitution.

entities.name: Mali
entities.snapshot: An al-Qaeda affiliate's fuel blockade cut Bamako's power to a few hours a day, while the junta dissolved political parties and tied itself ever closer to Russia.

entities.name: Malta
entities.snapshot: Robert Abela's Labour Party won a record fourth straight term in May 2026 in the EU's smallest member state, where rapid growth has strained housing and infrastructure.

entities.name: Myanmar
entities.snapshot: The junta held a widely dismissed election and made its leader president, but civil war goes on across much of the country five years after the coup.

entities.name: Montenegro
entities.snapshot: The frontrunner to become the EU's next member, aiming to close talks by 2026, in a small country still divided over its ties to Serbia.

entities.name: Mongolia
entities.snapshot: A ruling-party feud forced Prime Minister Zandanshatar out in March 2026, Mongolia's latest change of government in a democracy squeezed between Russia and China.

entities.name: Mozambique
entities.snapshot: Frelimo, in power since independence in 1975, kept the presidency after a disputed 2024 election and months of deadly protests, while an insurgency simmers in the gas-rich north.

entities.name: Mauritania
entities.snapshot: A Saharan republic that has stayed stable while its Sahel neighbours fell to coups and jihadists, now preparing to export offshore gas.

entities.name: Mauritius
entities.snapshot: A small island democracy that grew rich through sugar, textiles, tourism and finance, and recently secured sovereignty over the Chagos Islands from Britain.

entities.name: Malawi
entities.snapshot: Peter Mutharika returned to the presidency after beating Lazarus Chakwera in the September 2025 election, inheriting fuel shortages and very high inflation.

entities.name: Malaysia
entities.snapshot: Anwar Ibrahim's unity government faces corruption rows and ethnic tension ahead of an election due by early 2027.

entities.name: Namibia
entities.snapshot: A stable, sparsely populated democracy that elected its first woman president in 2024 and hopes new offshore oil and green hydrogen will tackle deep inequality.

entities.name: Niger
entities.snapshot: The junta that ousted Mohamed Bazoum in 2023 is fighting jihadists and hosting Russian troops, and blamed foreign leaders without evidence after a brazen attack on Niamey's airport.

entities.name: Nigeria
entities.snapshot: Africa's most populous country learned in January 2026 how close a 2025 coup plot came to killing its president, as insecurity spread across north and south.

entities.name: Nicaragua
entities.snapshot: Daniel Ortega and his wife Rosario Murillo now rule as co-presidents, preparing an open family succession as rumours about his health swirl.

entities.name: Netherlands
entities.snapshot: Rob Jetten became the Netherlands' youngest and first openly gay prime minister in February 2026, after his D66 overtook Geert Wilders' far right.

entities.name: Norway
entities.snapshot: Fights over new oil drilling and the oil fund's Israeli holdings nearly sank Labour's minority budget, which drew a record sum from the fund as the Iran war shook energy markets.

entities.name: Nepal
entities.snapshot: Six months after Gen Z protests burned parliament, a party founded in 2022 won a landslide and made a 35-year-old former rapper prime minister.

entities.name: Nauru
entities.snapshot: The world's smallest republic, a single island stripped by phosphate mining, which hosts Australia's offshore asylum processing and now sells citizenship to fund climate plans.

entities.name: New Zealand
entities.snapshot: Christopher Luxon's centre-right coalition faces voters on 7 November 2026, after a term of spending cuts and fights over the Treaty of Waitangi.

entities.name: Oman
entities.snapshot: The Gulf's quiet mediator, an absolute monarchy that has hosted US-Iran talks and stayed out of regional wars while diversifying away from oil.

entities.name: Pakistan
entities.snapshot: Pakistan brokered the US-Iran ceasefire and hosted the first direct talks in decades, while fighting its own war against the Taliban next door.

entities.name: Panama
entities.snapshot: Under pressure from Trump, Panama's Supreme Court voided Hong Kong's CK Hutchison's contracts for the canal's two main ports, and the state took them over with Maersk as temporary operator.

entities.name: Peru
entities.snapshot: Keiko Fujimori won the presidency on her fourth attempt in 2026, after a decade in which Congress removed or forced out president after president.

entities.name: Philippines
entities.snapshot: Vice President Sara Duterte went on trial in the Senate after a second impeachment, while a flood-control kickback scandal brought mass protests against the whole political class.

entities.name: Palau
entities.snapshot: A small, US-aligned island nation that recognises Taiwan and has offered to host more US military facilities.

entities.name: Papua New Guinea
entities.snapshot: Bougainville's parliament set 1 September 2027 for independence, putting James Marape's government on the spot in a nation of more than 800 languages.

entities.name: Poland
entities.snapshot: Nationalist President Karol Nawrocki has vetoed bill after bill from Donald Tusk's government, leaving its reform agenda stuck ahead of the 2027 election.

entities.name: North Korea
entities.snapshot: South Korean intelligence said in 2026 that Kim Jong Un's daughter had been designated his successor, as troops and shells sent to Russia brought the regime cash and combat experience.

entities.name: Portugal
entities.snapshot: Socialist António José Seguro beat far-right André Ventura by about two to one in February 2026's presidential runoff, the first time the far right reached a final round.

entities.name: Paraguay
entities.snapshot: A landlocked farm economy run by the conservative Colorado Party almost continuously since 1947, now led by Santiago Peña, a close Trump and Milei ally.

entities.name: Palestine
entities.snapshot: A year after the Gaza ceasefire, Hamas still governs the strip, and Abbas postponed the first Palestinian parliamentary election in nearly 20 years to 2027.

entities.name: Qatar
entities.snapshot: Iranian strikes knocked out about a sixth of Qatar's LNG export capacity, putting both its gas fortune and its role as everyone's mediator under fire.

entities.name: Romania
entities.snapshot: Spending cuts to tame the EU's biggest budget deficit tipped Romania into recession in 2026 and strained the coalition, as the far-right AUR waits in the wings.

entities.name: Russia
entities.snapshot: Putin's party took three-quarters of Duma seats in a September 2026 election with the anti-war Yabloko barred, as the war in Ukraine went on.

entities.name: Rwanda
entities.snapshot: A tightly controlled, fast-modernising state under Paul Kagame, rebuilt after the 1994 genocide and accused by the UN of backing M23 rebels in Congo.

entities.name: Saudi Arabia
entities.snapshot: Iranian missiles hit Riyadh and the oil heartland, then the Houthis broke their truce and struck Saudi cities, bringing the war MBS had worked to avoid to his doorstep.

entities.name: Sudan
entities.snapshot: The war between the army and the RSF, now in its fourth year, has caused the world's largest humanitarian crisis and effectively split the country in two.

entities.name: Senegal
entities.snapshot: The discovery of $13 billion in hidden debt froze an IMF programme and split the president from his own mentor, Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko.

entities.name: Singapore
entities.snapshot: Singapore's government warned that Asia was "particularly exposed" as oil prices jumped more than 60 percent during the Iran war, rattling a city that runs on trade.

entities.name: Solomon Islands
entities.snapshot: Parliament ousted Jeremiah Manele in a May 2026 no-confidence vote and chose opposition leader Matthew Wale, in a country courted by both China and Australia.

entities.name: Sierra Leone
entities.snapshot: A country rebuilt after a brutal civil war, now led by Julius Maada Bio, whose disputed 2023 re-election brought sanctions threats and a coup attempt.

entities.name: El Salvador
entities.snapshot: Nayib Bukele's gang crackdown made El Salvador one of the safest countries in the region, at the cost of mass detention and a near-total concentration of power.

entities.name: San Marino
entities.snapshot: One of the world's oldest republics, a hilltop microstate inside Italy that has signed an association agreement with the EU.

entities.name: Somalia
entities.snapshot: Parliament extended the president's term by a year to push through one-person-one-vote elections; the opposition and powerful federal states call his mandate expired.

entities.name: Serbia
entities.snapshot: Facing student-led protests, Aleksandar Vučić resigned the presidency in September 2026 to run for prime minister in a snap election on 25 October.

entities.name: South Sudan
entities.snapshot: The world's youngest country is sliding back toward civil war, with First Vice President Riek Machar on trial and elections set for December 2026 widely doubted.

entities.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
entities.snapshot: Africa's second-smallest country, two cocoa islands in the Gulf of Guinea, where governments often fall but power changes without bloodshed.

entities.name: Suriname
entities.snapshot: Suriname's first woman president, Jennifer Geerlings-Simons, took office in 2025 as the country prepares for an offshore oil boom.

entities.name: Slovakia
entities.snapshot: Robert Fico's government dismantled the anti-corruption prosecutor, softened the criminal code and targeted NGOs, drawing large protests and EU concern.

entities.name: Slovenia
entities.snapshot: A near-tie in the March 2026 election ended with populist Janez Janša back as prime minister for a fourth time.

entities.name: Sweden
entities.snapshot: Sweden's left-leaning bloc won a narrow majority in September 2026, but forming a government has dragged on, leaving Ulf Kristersson as caretaker.

entities.name: Eswatini
entities.snapshot: Africa's last absolute monarchy, where King Mswati III appoints the government and political parties cannot contest elections.

entities.name: Seychelles
entities.snapshot: Africa's richest country per head, a 115-island tourism state where Patrick Herminie's United Seychelles returned to power in October 2025.

entities.name: Syria
entities.snapshot: Ahmed al-Sharaa's new government won sanctions relief from Washington but fought the Kurdish-led SDF in January before a deal on merging them into the state.

entities.name: Chad
entities.snapshot: A Sahel state ruled by Mahamat Déby, who took over when his father was killed in 2021, jailed his main rival and broke a long military alliance with France.

entities.name: Togo
entities.snapshot: Faure Gnassingbé, whose family has ruled since 1967, switched to a parliamentary system that lets him stay in charge indefinitely as President of the Council.

entities.name: Thailand
entities.snapshot: Anutin Charnvirakul rode nationalist anger over the border war with Cambodia to a landslide in a snap election in early 2026.

entities.name: Tajikistan
entities.snapshot: Ruled since 1992 by Emomali Rahmon, who appears to be preparing his son to succeed him, in a remittance economy on the Afghan border.

entities.name: Turkmenistan
entities.snapshot: One of the world's most closed countries, sitting on huge gas reserves, where the former president handed power to his son and still rules alongside him.

entities.name: Timor-Leste
entities.snapshot: One of Asia's freest democracies, which became ASEAN's 11th member in 2025 but depends on a dwindling oil fund.

entities.name: Tonga
entities.snapshot: The Pacific's only kingdom chose a noble, Lord Fakafānua, as prime minister after the November 2025 election.

entities.name: Trinidad and Tobago
entities.snapshot: The Caribbean's energy powerhouse, where Kamla Persad-Bissessar returned as prime minister in 2025 and backed US strikes on Venezuelan boats nearby.

entities.name: Tunisia
entities.snapshot: The birthplace of the Arab Spring has slid back into one-man rule under Kais Saied, who dissolved parliament in 2021 and jailed many of his critics.

entities.name: Turkey
entities.snapshot: Istanbul's jailed mayor, Erdoğan's strongest rival, went on trial with 414 co-defendants while a court ousted the main opposition party's leader.

entities.name: Tuvalu
entities.snapshot: One of the countries most threatened by rising seas, which signed a treaty letting its citizens move to Australia and is building a digital copy of itself.

entities.name: Taiwan
entities.snapshot: An opposition-run legislature held up Taiwan's budget and weapons purchases for months under Chinese blockade drills, before Lai proposed a record defence budget.

entities.name: Tanzania
entities.snapshot: After a 2025 election with the main opposition barred and hundreds reported killed in protests, Samia Suluhu Hassan's government faces its worst crisis of legitimacy.

entities.name: Uganda
entities.snapshot: Yoweri Museveni, in power since 1986, won a seventh term in January 2026 against Bobi Wine, with his son and army chief positioned as heir.

entities.name: Ukraine
entities.snapshot: A brief US-brokered ceasefire in May collapsed within days, and the war ground on along a 745-mile front as both sides escalated long-range strikes.

entities.name: Uruguay
entities.snapshot: One of the world's most stable democracies, where centre-left Yamandú Orsi took office in 2025 in a smooth handover typical of Uruguayan politics.

entities.name: United States
entities.snapshot: Trump's approval has sunk below 40 percent ahead of the 3 November midterms, after a year of tariffs, an Iran war and a military raid that seized Venezuela's president.

entities.name: Uzbekistan
entities.snapshot: A Taliban-built canal set to divert up to a fifth of the Amu Darya's flow threatens Uzbekistan's cotton and wheat fields, testing Mirziyoyev's engagement with Kabul.

entities.name: Holy See (Vatican City)
entities.snapshot: The first American pope, Leo XIV, made artificial intelligence the theme of his first encyclical and declared the traditionalist Society of St Pius X in schism.

entities.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
entities.snapshot: Voters ended Ralph Gonsalves's 24 years in power in November 2025, handing the opposition NDP a landslide and making Godwin Friday prime minister.

entities.name: Venezuela
entities.snapshot: A US raid in January seized Nicolás Maduro and flew him to New York, but his vice president took over and Washington chose to deal with her rather than the opposition.

entities.name: Vietnam
entities.snapshot: To Lam, re-elected party chief in January 2026 and now also president, has become Vietnam's most powerful leader in decades while slashing the bureaucracy.

entities.name: Vanuatu
entities.snapshot: A Pacific nation rebuilding from a deadly December 2024 earthquake, which won a landmark advisory opinion on climate obligations from the International Court of Justice in 2025.

entities.name: Samoa
entities.snapshot: A proud Polynesian nation where La'auli Leuatea Schmidt's FAST party won a snap election in 2025 after splitting from the former prime minister.

entities.name: Kosovo
entities.snapshot: After repeated elections and deadlock, Kosovo finally chose a president in October 2026, weeks after a court convicted its wartime leader Hashim Thaçi.

entities.name: Yemen
entities.snapshot: Saudi Arabia crushed the UAE-backed southern separatists in January, then the Houthis broke their truce with Riyadh in July and struck Saudi cities and shipping.

entities.name: South Africa
entities.snapshot: The ANC-DA coalition faces its first big ballot test in the 4 November municipal elections, as voters weigh broken city services against national stability.

entities.name: Zambia
entities.snapshot: Hakainde Hichilema won a second term in August 2026 with about 61 percent, a reward for steering Zambia out of default and toward a copper boom.

entities.name: Zimbabwe
entities.snapshot: Emmerson Mnangagwa signed a constitutional change in 2026 keeping him in office until 2030, two years beyond his term, as ZANU-PF eyes even longer.

entities.name: Åland Islands
entities.note: Åland is an autonomous, Swedish-speaking, demilitarised region of Finland.

entities.name: Cook Islands
entities.note: The Cook Islands govern themselves in free association with New Zealand, whose citizenship islanders hold. A 2025 partnership deal with China strained that relationship.

entities.name: Curaçao
entities.note: Curaçao is a territory of the Netherlands. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for the Netherlands.

entities.name: Cayman Islands
entities.note: Cayman Is. is a territory of the United Kingdom. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for the United Kingdom.

entities.name: Western Sahara
entities.note: Western Sahara is a disputed territory. Morocco controls most of it and calls it its southern provinces; the Polisario Front, backed by Algeria, claims it as the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic. The UN still lists it as a non-self-governing territory.

entities.name: Falkland Islands
entities.note: The Falkland Islands are a self-governing British overseas territory, also claimed by Argentina, which lost a war over them in 1982.

entities.name: Faroe Islands
entities.note: Faeroe Is. is a territory of Denmark. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for Denmark.

entities.name: Guernsey
entities.note: Guernsey is a territory of the United Kingdom. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for the United Kingdom.

entities.name: Greenland
entities.note: Greenland is a self-governing part of the Kingdom of Denmark, with its own parliament and control over most domestic affairs. Copenhagen still runs its defence and foreign policy, which is why Trump's talk of buying or taking it lands on Denmark's desk.

entities.name: Guam
entities.note: Guam is a territory of the United States. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for the United States.

entities.name: Hong Kong
entities.note: Hong Kong is a special administrative region of China. The 'one country, two systems' arrangement promised it autonomy until 2047, but the 2020 National Security Law brought it firmly under Beijing's political control.

entities.name: Heard Island and McDonald Islands
entities.note: Heard I. and McDonald Is. is a territory of Australia. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for Australia.

entities.note: Isle of Man is a territory of the United Kingdom. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for the United Kingdom.

entities.name: Jersey
entities.note: Jersey is a territory of the United Kingdom. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for the United Kingdom.

entities.name: Macau
entities.note: Macao is a special administrative region of China and the world's biggest gambling hub by revenue. It has been governed closely in line with Beijing since its handover from Portugal in 1999.

entities.name: Saint Martin
entities.note: St-Martin is a territory of France. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for France.

entities.name: Northern Mariana Islands
entities.note: N. Mariana Is. is a territory of the United States. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for the United States.

entities.name: Montserrat
entities.note: Montserrat is a territory of the United Kingdom. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for the United Kingdom.

entities.name: New Caledonia
entities.note: New Caledonia is a French overseas collectivity in the Pacific, rich in nickel. Deadly riots in 2024 over voting rules reopened the long fight over independence between the Indigenous Kanak and settlers' descendants.

entities.name: Norfolk Island
entities.note: Norfolk Island is a territory of Australia. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for Australia.

entities.name: Niue
entities.note: Niue is a self-governing island in free association with New Zealand, with about 1,700 residents and far more Niueans living in New Zealand.

entities.name: Pitcairn Islands
entities.note: Pitcairn Is. is a territory of the United Kingdom. It doesn't get its own write-up; its politics run through the entry for the United Kingdom.

entities.name: Puerto Rico
entities.note: Puerto Rico is a US territory. Its 3.2 million people are US citizens but have no vote for president and only a non-voting delegate in Congress, and the island's status (statehood, independence or the current arrangement) is still argued over.
